text:
Mira: Heads-up — opened a PR to unify pagination + retry snippets across py/ts/go. fixes streaming examples and updates backoff guidance. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482
Alex: thanks — pinging for review. rough ETA?
Mira: hoping for quick reviews today, CI mostly green except one go snippet lint.
Sam: skimmed locally. two notes: the python async iterator should show transient retry handling, and TS should include both `for await` and the callback stream example.
Alex: I left an inline suggestion to prefer exponential backoff with full jitter (see our util `retryWithJitter`). small nit: avoid `time.sleep` in async snippet.
Owen: CI failure is from the Go example — unused `fmt` import in the snippet. I'll push a quick fix.
Mira: pushed commit to remove fmt and tweak wording. I also replaced the cursor example with a resumption-token pattern per migration guide. snippet preview below.
```python
# paginated streaming with transient retries (py)
async for page in client.responses.stream_pagination(prompt, cursor=None):
    try:
        for token in page.tokens:
            handle(token)
    except TransientError:
        # use our retry helper to avoid blocking the event loop
        await retry_with_jitter(lambda: client.responses.resume(page.cursor))
```
Sam: nice. for TS I added a concise generator example and a streaming callback variant. posted a commit suggestion for types in the SDK call.
```ts
// async generator style
for await (const page of client.responses.streamPagination({ prompt })) {
  page.tokens.forEach(t => processToken(t))
}
```
Alex: also suggest adding a one-line note about cursor TTL semantics in the migration docs — folks hit that in-prod.
Docs-bot: link-checker: 3/4 examples validated, one go-snippet flagged for formatting (fixed by Owen).
Owen: pushed go snippet fix (removed fmt, used strings.Builder). re-running CI.
Mira: CI passed on latest push. ready to merge after Alex approval.
Alex: LGTM, left one tiny wording nit on the retry paragraph. approving now :thumbsup:
Mira: thanks — merging and will backport to release/v1.8. adding a brief note in CHANGELOG about the pagination parity changes.
Sam: can you add a short line in the migration guide about explicit cursor resume vs implicit page offsets? customers asked about it.
Mira: will add a paragraph + example and link to the eval that caught the regression.
Alex: great. after merge I'll coordinate a small email to integrations channel about the snippet updates.
Mira: perfect — thanks team!
